The `{% extends %}`, `{% block %}`, and `{{ block.super }}` logic all live in this one file. `ExtendsNode.render` fills a `BlockContext` with the child's block nodes, then renders the parent. `BlockNode.render` pops the most-derived override for its name from that context, and `BlockNode.super()` re-renders the next-less-derived block from the same context.

`django/template/loader_tags.py` is the only file that implements this. The `{% block %}` tag, `BlockContext`, `ExtendsNode`, and `{{ block.super }}` are all defined there.

`ExtendsNode.render` (around line 134) first adds the child's `BlockNode`s to a shared `BlockContext`, then adds the root parent's blocks. Each block name gets a stack of implementations, and `get_block` returns the most-derived one. When the parent layout reaches a `BlockNode`, `BlockNode.render` pops the most-derived version and renders it. `BlockNode.super()` (line 71) checks whether another version of the same block is still on the stack. If one is, it renders that version and returns the output as safe HTML. If not, it returns an empty string. The method pushes the popped version back afterwards, so the stack stays intact for later blocks.
